category_title: Students who engage in high social interaction but require frequent off-task redirection
minimal_context: The student is assigned to work on a collaborative social studies task with peers in a mixed-age classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please start working on your collaborative social studies task as a team.

STUDENT: I'm just going to work independently on my section. We can just fit all the pieces together in the end.

TUTOR: Remember, this is supposed to be a team effort. Try talking to your group.

STUDENT: Communicating with them is tedious. I get 'easily frustrated' and have a 'hard time' working with others.

TUTOR: You need to help your peers with the assignment.

STUDENT: I don't want to be 'dragged down' by everyone else because I normally work faster. I know it's my 'stubbornness', but I'm doing this on my own.

options.A: Consistently seat the student in the front, wall-side row to minimize disturbances during collaborative tasks.
options.B: Consistently implement PIES principles: positive interdependence, individual accountability, equal participation, and simultaneous interaction during tasks.
options.C: Consistently contact the student's parents with praise regarding their performance on the collaborative social studies tasks.
options.D: Consistently implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the collaborative social studies tasks.
